story: Alaska Airlines was the first airline to adopt Air Space Intelligence's Flyways machine-learning route-optimization tool, and that Alaska deployment became the demonstration case behind the FAA's $875 million contract with the same company to build SMART, a predictive system to modernize the national airspace

claims.claim: The FAA awarded Air Space Intelligence an $875 million contract to modernize the national airspace system
claims.evidence: ASI Awarded $875m FAA contract to modernize the National Airspace System

claims.claim: The FAA contract with Air Space Intelligence is worth $875 million
claims.evidence: The FAA is so convinced that it recently announced an $875 million contract with Air Space Intelligence to modernize the nation's airspace.

claims.claim: The FAA award to Air Space Intelligence is a 12 year contract
The new FAA system is named SMART for Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories
claims.evidence: SMART system, short for Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes, and Trajectories

claims.claim: The contract also covers the Flow Management Data and Services platform known as FMDS
claims.evidence: Flow Management Data and Services, or FMDS, platform

claims.claim: The FAA targeted an initial operational deployment of SMART in fall 2026
claims.evidence: The FAA has targeted an initial operational deployment of SMART in fall 2026.

claims.claim: Alaska Airlines was the first airline to start using the Flyways system in 2021
claims.evidence: Alaska was the first airline to start using the Flyways system back in 2021

claims.claim: Alaska Airlines operates roughly 1,500 flights on a typical day
claims.evidence: On a typical day, Alaska Airlines operates roughly 1,500 flights

claims.claim: Alaska Airlines says Flyways saves it roughly a million gallons of fuel per year
claims.evidence: Alaska says it's saving tens of thousands of hours in the air and roughly a million gallons of fuel per year because of Flyways.

claims.claim: Alaska Airlines says Flyways saves it tens of thousands of hours in the air
claims.evidence: Alaska says it's saving tens of thousands of hours in the air and roughly a million gallons of fuel per year because of Flyways.

claims.evidence: Optimized routes using Flyways saved over 1.2 million gallons of fuel, equivalent to 11,958 metric tons of CO2 emissions.

claims.claim: Flyways generates optimized route recommendations for dispatchers and pilots that are safe, ATC compliant, minimize fuel, reduce flight time, and avoid congested airspace
claims.evidence: Flyways AI then generates optimized route recommendations for dispatchers and pilots that are safe, ATC compliant, minimize fuel consumption, reduce flight time and avoid potentially congested airspace.

claims.claim: Flyways analyzes air traffic, wind, weather and other factors to anticipate what will happen during flight before it does
claims.evidence: analyzing air traffic, wind, weather and other factors to anticipate what is going to happen during flight before it does

record_does_not_say: The record does not state the exact date the FAA award was signed. No fetched page gives a signing date; ExecutiveBiz published the award on June 23, 2026, which is why the sources carry that date.

The record does not confirm the 12 year contract term or the fall 2026 initial deployment against a primary FAA document. Both rest on ExecutiveBiz alone and are reported rather than verified against the government record.

The record does not verify the award through a federal government document. SAM.gov and USAspending.gov were not reachable this run; the $875 million figure is corroborated across NPR, ExecutiveBiz and Air Space Intelligence's own site.

The 1.2 million gallon figure is from Alaska Airlines' 2024 newsroom and covers an unspecified period, so it is background, not the in-window number. The current figure the deck uses is NPR's roughly one million gallons per year, attributed to Alaska Airlines.
